title: A healer in name, death in practice
literal_meaning: Dhanvantari in name; Yama in treatment.
meaning_odia: ନାଆଁରେ ଧନ୍ୱନ୍ତରୀଙ୍କ ପରି ବଡ଼ ବୈଦ୍ୟ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଚିକିତ୍ସାରେ ଯମଙ୍କ ପରି—ଏହି ବିପରୀତ ଚିତ୍ର କଥକଙ୍କ କଟାକ୍ଷ। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଏହା ସୁନାମ କିମ୍ବା ଉପାଧି ଥାଇ ମଧ୍ୟ କାମରେ ଉପକାର ବଦଳରେ କ୍ଷତି କରିବାକୁ କହେ। ମୂଳର ଚିକିସ୍ରାରେ ଶବ୍ଦକୁ ଅର୍ଥ ଓ ବ୍ୟାକରଣ ଆଧାରରେ ଚିକିତ୍ସାରେ ବୋଲି ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ଅନୁମାନରେ ସୁଧାରାଯାଇଛି।
explanation: The first name promises healing; the second turns that promise into its opposite. Our editorial reading hears a sharp criticism of someone whose impressive reputation conceals work that causes harm. The contrast is stronger than simple failure to live up to a title.
usage_example: Original imagined example: A celebrated repair expert makes a machine worse while claiming to restore it. A disappointed customer recalls the contrast between a healer’s name and harmful practice.
cultural_context: Dhanvantari supplies the image of healing and Yama the image of death. Placing these names on either side of a single practitioner makes the satire immediate: the advertised role and the actual effect pull in opposite directions.
